@arankomatsuzaki @julesgm4 @NafiseSadat It's hard to draw a sharp border between NLU skills and more general AI skills, but we've tried to focus on tasks that require only very small amounts of reasoning/knowledge beyond that which is minimally necessary to understand common language.

@arankomatsuzaki @julesgm4 @NafiseSadat I guess I just don't think of that as NLU. It's an interesting/worthwhile direction to work on toward general conversational AI, but we've been focused on _just_ understanding what a text is meant to convey.

@sandyasm @srchvrs @julesgm4 We looked at these for SuperGLUE, but couldn't find any public datasets that seemed reasonably difficult. It seems like an area where a lot of work happens on proprietary data.

@sir_deenicus Yeah, these are definitely big open question. The focus on inference time is meant to fit into the energy consumption/CO2 emissions focus of the workshop—I bet we could see a lot of progress on that in the very short term with improvements to methods like distillation.

@julesgm4 On a related note, though, we are helping @NafiseSadat et al. put together a shared task for *highly efficient* NLU models, but the goals there are somewhat different from the how-well-can-you-do orientation of plain SuperGLUE. Context: https://t.co/sDEpwqMtpF

@julesgm4 I still believe we can do interesting work with IID test sets if we have high-enough quality data and aim high enough, so maybe we'll revisit this in a year or two if the NLU dataset landscape changes much...

@julesgm4 Another interesting option is adaptive evaluations using ideas like adversarial filtering or build-it-break-it-style shared tasks. It's hard to make that as fair or as user-friendly as a simple shared task with a fixed test set. I bet it can be done, but I don't know how.
@julesgm4 So, where could one go? Generation/structured prediction is an obvious and reasonable direction, but I think that's just a different problem—NLU is still interesting and unsolved.
@julesgm4 ...but I'm not sure that we've accumulated a big/diverse enough set over the last nine months that we'd be able to create something much harder than SuperGLUE in the same style.

@julesgm4 The biggest lesson we learned from creating SuperGLUE is that most 'typical' NLU datasets are already solved at human level. We left out a *lot* of tasks (many of which looked hard a priori) for that reason. The community is getting better at dataset creation...
@julesgm4 We aren't at the moment. My coauthors might feel differently, but I don't think there's a straightforward way to do it.

We urge researchers studying similar questions not to put too much weight on the qualitative conclusions from any one experiment of this kind, and to use more than one method whenever possible.

These are all reasonable ways of operationalizing the research question we're interested in and we tried them all. They don't give strictly contradictory answers, but the qualitative conclusions that they suggest point in substantially different directions.

Do you probe model hidden states for features that reflect the knowledge you're interested in? For LM-style models like BERT, do you look at word predictions/likelihoods that are relevant to what you're interested in?

So, do you look at raw model accuracy on test data that highlights this phenomenon? Do you look at the relative label probabilities of paired examples that vary in a way that isolates the phenomenon? ...
